blocks.text: Seller net proceeds calculator: estimate what you would walk away with

faq.a: The page's answer: generally for one or more of three reasons — it is overpriced relative to comparable recent sales and current competition, it is not marketed well enough online and offline, or it does not show well; the fix starts with a home evaluation and an honest comparison against recent sales, active listings and expired or terminated listings.

faq.q: Do I need a REALTOR® to sell my home in BC?
faq.a: No — BCFSA's licensing guidance confirms a person does not require a licence to provide real estate services to themselves, such as selling their own property; a licence (or an exemption) is required to provide real estate services to or on behalf of another person for remuneration.

faq.q: What are the costs of selling a home in BC?
faq.a: The page lists real estate commission (split between the listing agent and the buyer's agent), cleaning, staging and preparation, legal fees and disbursements, and a possible mortgage penalty if the mortgage is broken early — and states no commission figure, which BCFSA's framework places in the listing conversation, where a licensee must give consumers information about commissions and fees.

faq.q: Do I have to accept an offer on my home?
faq.a: The page's answer: no — on receiving an offer you can accept it as-is, counter, or reject it altogether; a counter voids the previous offer. Read your own listing contract's stated terms before relying on any general statement about when an offer must be accepted, and take that question to your agent or lawyer.

faq.q: Who pays the property transfer tax when I sell?
faq.a: The buyer: PTT is payable by the purchaser on the fair market value of the property on the day it is registered at the Land Title Office — when you buy your next home, you pay it as the buyer.
